newsitem.title: USA: Bill to ban cheap U.S.-made handguns proposed.
newsitem.headline: Bill to ban cheap U.S.-made handguns proposed.

text.p: A bill to ban the production and sale of cheap American-made hand guns was proposed on Thursday by several Senate and House gun control advocates.
"This bill is aimed at junk guns -- the cheap, unsafe and easily concealable handguns that are the criminals' clear favourite," Sen. Barbara Boxer said at a news conference with three other senators.
"Under our bill, junk guns will no longer be allowed to be manufactured or sold in the United States of America," the California Democrat added.

She was joined by Rhode Island Republican John Chafee and Democrats Dick Durbin of Illinois and Jack Reed of Rhode Island. Representative Charles Schumer, D-New York, will introduce the bill in the House.

It would place the same safety and quality standards on handguns made in the United States that are imposed on imported handguns. Currently, U.S.-made handguns do not have to meet any federal standards.
"Something is wrong when Cabbage Patch dolls have to meet tougher safety standards than guns," Durbin said.
"Clearly, handguns are widely available -- often, too widely available. They are wreaking havoc on our streets and in our homes," Chafee said.
The bill was endorsed by Sarah Brady, chair of the gun control group Handgun Control, and several police chiefs.
